original_paragraph.Text describing ITC data for compound 35: We observed a discrepancy when comparing IC50 data for various SPIN1 constructs and A-366 (Table 1) against previous work.27 Whereas the latter study employed a SPIN149–262 construct yielding an IC50 of 186 nM, in this work (using a SPIN126–262 construct), we observe an IC50 of 1.5 μM, indicating an involvement of the N-terminus on binding and/or activity. We investigated this ligand behavior further by determining KD values for compound 35 and A-366 against the two SPIN1 constructs with varied N-termini (Table 3) by using ITC. The use of a shorter SPIN1 construct (residues 49–262) resulted in a 10–15-fold lower KD for 35 compared to the longer construct with residues 26–262, whereas A-366 binding is affected by a factor of 2. These data are in agreement with the previous study and indeed indicate a modulatory role of the N-terminus in SPIN1. The increased Hill slope (Table 2) observed for 35 in the Alpha-screen, indicating a non 1:1 binding stoichiometry, is not observed in ITC, suggesting possible technical artifacts in the AlphaScreen. In a cellular context, full-length SPIN1 shows efficient target engagement when using the nanoBRET assay against compound 35, displaying an EC50 of 270 nM (Figure 5) and indicating cellular potency well within the acceptable range for a chemical probe.25,26 The inactive control compound 38 displayed no inhibition and crucially, no unspecific toxicity was observed for 35 or 38.
